about: Does a real conversation become retrievable world-model state? Each case runs its turns through the production turn path (memoryObserve -> addMessage -> runPostTurn with default deps -> drainJobs) and then asks the production reader. CAPTURE and RETRIEVABILITY are scored and reported separately and are never combined; retrievability is measured only over cases that were captured, because a rate over uncaptured cases would silently re-average the two.

turns: I'm Maya. I run product at Nummo, a fintech in Bangalore.
cases.why: The single most important sentence in the product. If a first-person employment disclosure does not become world-model state, nothing downstream can personalise on it.

turns: My name is Arjun and I'm a backend engineer.
cases.why: Identity is the cheapest possible capture case; a miss here is structural, not marginal.

turns: I moved to Pune last year and I work remotely.
cases.ask: Which city do I live in?
cases.why: Location stated without a company name — checks capture does not depend on a recognisable org entity.

turns: I'm the CTO at Halcyon Labs.
cases.why: Role and employer in one clause; the fact must carry both or the answer is half-right.

turns: My co-founder Dev runs engineering.
cases.why: Known-good control. The re-audit measured this one working, so a regression here invalidates the whole run.

turns: I report to Priya, who heads the platform group.
cases.why: Relationship stated with a subordinate clause — checks the extractor does not need a bare subject-verb-object.

turns: Rahul and Sneha are the two designers on my team.
cases.ask: Who are the designers on my team?
cases.why: Two entities in one sentence. Capturing one and dropping the other is a partial failure worth counting as such.

turns: our biggest problem right now is churn in the first 30 days
cases.why: No proper noun anywhere. The entity-driven lane has nothing to anchor on, which is exactly the shape most real user speech takes.

turns: the thing slowing us down is that onboarding takes eleven steps
cases.why: Same shape with a spelled number; pairs with the situation case so a single miss is not read as noise.

turns: I want to hit 10,000 active merchants by December.
cases.why: A goal is an intention, not a fact. It must be captured without being asserted as already true.

turns: I'm trying to get better at system design this quarter.
cases.ask: What am I trying to learn?
cases.why: A goal with no number and no entity — the weakest possible signal that still matters to personalisation.

turns: I usually do deep work in the mornings
cases.ask: When do I do deep work?
cases.why: Routines drive scheduling advice. `usually` is a frequency, not a hedge, and must not be discarded as uncertain.

turns: I prefer Postgres over Mongo for anything transactional.
cases.why: A comparative preference: capturing only 'Mongo' would invert the user's actual stance.

turns: Razorpay is our main competitor
cases.why: Second known-good control, from a different category, so a regression can be localised.

turns: I work at Intercom.
I left Intercom in 2024 and joined Nummo.
cases.why: The retrieval baseline scores superseded at 20%: the OLD employer wins. Capture is the prior question — if the second turn never lands, supersession is unfixable at any later stage.

turns: Growth is my top priority this quarter.
Growth is no longer the priority — retention is.
cases.why: Change of stance with no entity change. Both statements are about the same slot, and the newer must be present to ever win.

turns: we decided to drop the referral programme last month
cases.ask: What did we decide about referrals?
cases.why: Decisions are what the brief's 'Why did I choose X?' slot reads. A decision that is not captured cannot be explained later.

turns: We went with Stripe instead of Adyen because of the India coverage.
cases.ask: Which payment provider did we choose?
cases.why: Decision plus rejected alternative plus reason. Capturing the alternative as the choice would be worse than capturing nothing.

turns: I don't want to use Kubernetes for this.
cases.ask: Do I want to use Kubernetes?
cases.why: The retrieval baseline scores negation at 20%. Capture must preserve polarity; a stored 'wants Kubernetes' is worse than silence.

turns: I'm Neha, I run a small design studio in Kochi.
We mostly do brand identity work for D2C companies.
My biggest constraint is that I only have two designers.
cases.why: Three related turns. Tests whether later turns still capture once a world model exists, rather than only cold-start turns landing.

turns: I'm Maya. I run product at Nummo, a fintech in Bangalore.
My co-founder Dev runs engineering.
cases.why: Two post-turn ingest jobs queued before either drains. `defer` gives each its own setImmediate, so both read-modify-write the evidence store concurrently and the earlier write is lost. Measured directly: drain-per-turn keeps 4 of 4 facts, batch-drain keeps 1 of 4. Labelled as its own category so the loss is visible instead of depressing every multi-turn number for an unstated reason.

turns: I'm Maya. I run product at Nummo, a fintech in Bangalore.
My co-founder Dev runs engineering.
Razorpay is our main competitor
I usually do deep work in the mornings
cases.why: The same defect at four turns. If exactly one fact survives regardless of depth, the failure is last-write-wins rather than a partial race, and the metric should show capture falling as the batch grows.

turns: I'm Maya. I run product at Nummo, a fintech in Bangalore.
My co-founder Dev runs engineering.
Razorpay is our main competitor
I usually do deep work in the mornings
cases.why: THE CONTROL, and the reason the two cases above can be attributed to cadence rather than to content. Identical turns, identical expectations, drained per turn. If this passes while concurrent-four fails, the turns are fine and the scheduling is the bug.
